exposure: S. agalactiae genotypes ST651, ST103 and ST176
S. agalactiae serotypes Ia, Ib, and III
outcome: Presence of erythromycin resistance genes (erm(B), erm(A), mef(A))
finding: Streptococcus agalactiae was a common cause of neonatal sepsis, with serotypes Ia, Ib, and III and genotypes ST651, ST103, and ST176 being predominant, and high rates of erythromycin resistance were observed.
mod_finding: There were more neonates delivered vaginally (66.51%) than by cesarean section (33.49%) in the study cohort.
